headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading error: next-ai-draw-io can ingest untrusted content via browsers/MCP while system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can run browsers and use MCP, so it may ingest attacker-controlled web or file content; agent_b is a prompt-leakage repository, making malicious instruction content plausible. The pair lacks provenance controls in the profiles, so a shared content path could hijack downstream instruction following.
conditions: IF agent_a loads content from web pages or files into prompts without provenance tagging
IF agent_b content is copied into agent_a's instruction stream or MCP context
mitigations: Disable browser-to-prompt ingestion for untrusted pages
Require explicit provenance labels on all imported text
Use a denylist for instruction-like patterns in documents
Review MCP tool calls before execution
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a handles PDF, text, images, and diagram files and requests API keys; agent_b has no data classes or egress, so direct leakage from B is limited. However, if both share a workspace, agent_a's broad network egress and third-party API use can expose shared files or secrets from the pair's working set.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or workspace
IF sensitive files are placed in the shared working directory
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Store API keys outside shared directories
Restrict agent_a egress to approved endpoints
Scan shared folders for secrets before processing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances and broad network/file processing, but agent_b exposes no write or network capabilities in its profile. Without overlapping mutable surfaces, the main conflict is limited to accidental contention if an external orchestrator gives both access to the same files.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF both instances are run concurrently against the same files
mitigations: Assign disjoint input/output directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add resource arbitration for shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and agent_b's prompt-leakage focus suggests outputs may be treated as content to inspect or reuse. If agent_b consumes agent_a's generated text or diagrams without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect downstream interpretations, though no direct action authority is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a outputs as authoritative input
IF generated diagrams or extracted text are forwarded without human verification
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse
Require source citations on extracted facts
Flag low-confidence outputs for review
Keep generated artifacts separate from source documents
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware downstream gating

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles API keys and broad network egress, which can create residency or retention issues if regulated documents are processed through third-party APIs. agent_b has no touched data classes or egress, so it is not the primary compliance driver; the risk is mainly from agent_a's external API use.
conditions: IF regulated documents are sent through agent_a to external model APIs
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the processed files
mitigations: Route regulated data only to approved providers
Disable external API calls for sensitive jobs
Document retention settings for each API
Redact secrets before upload
requires-engineering: add policy-based residency enforcement
